about: Control points for the AD 1 coast (M3b; tools/map/coast-ad1.mjs, npm run map:coast-ad1). Kept apart from tools/map/coast-anchors.json so the 1219 field's fingerprint does not move. A 'group' with the name of a 1219 group REPLACES that group's k for AD 1 (its points are fitted again with the older ones added); groups of 1219 that are not named here keep their k. 'value' points are fitted, 'check' points only compared. Heights are metres above today's mean sea level in each study's own datum. Ages in cal BP are years before 1950 (AD = 1950 - cal BP, so 2205 cal BP is 255 BC, written -255). The AD 1 sea height is then a straight line in time from AD 1 to the 1219 value (src/sim/coast-date.js lead-in).

uppland-north.about: North Uppland (Forsmark area). The 1219 fit used Eckarfjärden alone; for AD 1 the two older lake isolations of Hedenström and Risberg are fitted instead, and Eckarfjärden (1100) is only compared. The plain uplift rule is about 2 m too low at AD 1 here (about 12 m against about 14 to 15 m).

points.place: Lake Eckarfjärden, near Forsmark, north Uppland (the same point as in coast-anchors.json)
points.source: Hedenström, A. and Risberg, J. (2003), Shore displacement in northern Uppland during the last 6500 calendar years, SKB Technical Report TR-03-17

tallinn.about: Kopli (Tallinn): Kakumäe joined the mainland about 2800 cal BP, Kopli about 1000 years later (about AD 150) (Saarse and Vassiljev 2010). GEBCO's heights at 450 m cannot show the narrow low neck of the Kopli peninsula, so the island is a HAND-DRAWN CUT: the cells under the line below are sea until the year given and land after it. The line's place (across the low ground that joins the peninsula to the mainland, about 59.4465N from 24.655E to 24.725E, and carried on along the same line in both directions until it meets today's sea) is our own reading of today's map, not the paper's map: TO CHECK. It stands for an estimate, not a survey.

kopliPeninsula.place: the middle of the Kopli peninsula (our own reading of today's map, TO CHECK)

mainland.place: Tallinn old town, on the mainland

tallinn.source: Saarse, L. and Vassiljev, J. (2010), Holocene shore displacement in the surroundings of Tallinn, North Estonia, Estonian Journal of Earth Sciences 59(3), 207-215, doi:10.3176/earth.2010.3.03

older: Not used: Lohja 6.23 m at 2240 cal BP (its place in the Rosentau database is not yet read, TO CHECK) and Prassi on Hiiumaa (a limiting point). SGU's shore model (resource.sgu.se) is blocked: Sweden's AD 1 shore is the estimate, as in 1219.
